# agents/

<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by doc-sync. Edit Purpose and Key Patterns freely — they are preserved on update. -->

## Purpose

Three autonomous LangGraph agents that drive the L-ESCROW lifecycle end-to-end. Buyer posts RFPs from the sandbox issue backlog, Seller bids and generates LLM code fixes, Assessor runs a dual-judge jury on the diff and settles escrow.

## Files

- `assessor.py`: Polls Locked RFPs → builds unified diff → calls Judge A (Llama 3.3) + Judge B (Gemma 2) concurrently → unanimous settle or HITL conflict
- `buyer.py`: Fetches unresolved sandbox issues → posts one RFP per issue via POST /api/v1/rfp
- `runner.py`: Entry point — runs all three agents with asyncio.gather()
- `seller.py`: Scores Open RFPs at 85% margin → bids → calls Groq to generate code fix → writes to prs/

## Key Patterns

- All agents communicate with Hub via HTTP only (`httpx`) — never import `db.py` directly
- LangGraph `StateGraph` with `TypedDict` state; every node returns `{**state, ...updated fields}`
- Seller writes raw Python fix to `prs/pr_{seller_id}_{rfp_id}.py` — strips markdown fences if present
- Assessor skips cycle if `sandbox_file` set but no PR file found yet (retries on next poll)
- `FORCE_VERDICT_A` / `FORCE_VERDICT_B` env vars override LLM calls for testing

## Dependencies

- `groq` SDK — same `GROQ_API_KEY` used for Seller fix generation and both Assessor judges
- `httpx` — async HTTP to Hub
- `langgraph` — StateGraph orchestration
- `SIMULATION_PATH` env var (default: `backend/simulation_sandbox/`)

## Notes

- Judge B uses `gemma2-9b-it` (not llama) — both judges share the same Groq key
- Runner polls: Buyer 15s, Seller 8s, Assessor 5s
- Without `DEMO_MODE=true` on server, bids won't lock (real Locus payment required)
- Run server with `--reload-exclude "*/simulation_sandbox/*"` to prevent reload on PR file writes
